question: Ross (2012) Table 4 (pp. 1274-1275), all PAn consonants in 20 Formosan languages: what is entered beside the rows of the language sources and of Ross (2015)?
chosen_reading: Only the cells of lects that had no row at all for the phoneme: Taokas (*b, *q, *j, *m, *n, *L, *l), Papora (*p, *b, *t, *q, *j, *m, *n, *L, *l, *R), Hoanya (the same ten), Favorlang *x, Proto-Atayal *Z and *D, Siraya (*p, *b, *C, *k, *-y, *j, *m, *ŋ, *L, *l, *R) and Amis (*C, *Z, *D, *j; on Proto-Amis-Sakizaya), the last two stated against PAn (parent_lect_id pan) because the lects stand under Proto-East Formosan. Cells that repeat a phoneme the lect already has a row for were not compared symbol by symbol.
alternatives: 1. Enter every cell as a second source. 2. Enter *ñ (Puyuma l, Tsou n, Kanakanavu ŋ, Saaroa ɬ, Saisiyat l, Siraya l, Kavalan n): the default PAn inventory has no *ñ. 3. Enter Basay, Trobiawan and Kavalan: they stand under Proto-Basay and Proto-Kavalan (decision tseng-nef), and Tseng's (2023) Table 6.4 takes its Taokas and Saisiyat columns from this table. 4. Table 9 (p. 1311), the reflexes that keep *z, *d, *Z, *D apart: the rows of Ross (2015) have them.

question: Gap audit of 26 November 2026, §1: Walworth (2014) and Li (1985) have no rows. Are their tables entered?
chosen_reading: Not in this batch. Walworth (2014): Tables 1, 4, 7, 10, 11 and 12 are taken or adapted from Marck (2000: 24-26, 45, 132-134), whose rows are entered from the original; Tables 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 13 are word lists. What is Walworth's own is her judgement of Marck's sporadic changes (five of the six PCEP changes kept, *kumi > *kumu rejected; five of the six Proto-Marquesic and eight of the ten Proto-Tahitic changes questioned, pp. 262-265), which is not on the rows. Li (1985): Table 2 (pp. 261-262 and following) gives the reflexes of the PAN consonants (in Dyen's symbols *D, *d', *Z, *g', *γ) in some thirty Formosan dialects (five Atayal, three Sediq, Tsou, Kanakanavu, Saaroa, three Rukai, two Bunun, Paiwan, two Puyuma, Thao, Saisiyat, Pazeh, Kavalan, two Amis, Taokas, Babuza, Papora, Hoanya, Siraya); it was looked at on one page image and not read.
alternatives: Mark Marck's rows that Walworth questions as disputed, with her page. Enter Li's (1985) Table 2 for the dialects that are lects, from enlarged page images.
